```{r}

#| label: create-intensity-matrices

#Make everything for limma to process
G_matrix <- do.call(cbind, map(arrayList, "G"))
Gb_matrix <- do.call(cbind, map(arrayList, "Gb"))
R_matrix <- do.call(cbind, map(arrayList, "R"))
Rb_matrix <- do.call(cbind, map(arrayList, "Rb"))
dim(G_matrix)


#There were some problems with using the package directly to do this... the the 
#matrix was construted manually... 

RG <- new(
  "RGList",
  list(
    R = R_matrix,
    G = G_matrix,
    Rb = Rb_matrix,
    Gb = Gb_matrix,

    genes = data.frame(
      Spot = spotLabels
    ),

    targets = data.frame(
      FileName = basename(rawFiles),
      SampleID = sampleIDs
    )
  )
)
#They are inserted to every data table in the limma data structure
rownames(RG) <- spotLabels
colnames(RG) <- sampleIDs

class(RG)
dim(RG)

```

```{r}

#| label: inspect-annotation

#We want to use the annotation becuase we will later want to distinguish
#the control probes for normalization purposes
annotation <- read_tsv(file = "../data/_raw/annotation.tsv") |> 
  as_tibble()

#See the annotation table
glimpse(annotation)
colnames(annotation)
head(annotation)
stopifnot(all(spotLabels %in% annotation$SPOT_LABELS))

#Standarize the annotation table with the right spotLabels title
spotTable <- tibble(Spot = spotLabels)
annotationPrepared <- spotTable |>
  left_join(annotation, by = c("Spot" = "SPOT_LABELS"))

#Put the gene annotation into the data object
RG$genes <- as.data.frame(annotationPrepared)

```

```{r}
boxplot(

)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))


```

```{r}
#| label: background-correction
#| message: FALSE

#Correct for the background noise using normexp (authors did the same)
#Can manage background higher than measurment... uses normal distribution to model noise
RG_corrected <- RG |>
  backgroundCorrect(
    method = "normexp",
    offset = 0
  )

#Checks that no negative signal is present
sum(RG_corrected$G <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(RG_corrected$R <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
```

Normalization:

```{r}

#| label: extract-grid-layout

#The authors performed a "print-tip LOESS normalization" which is a normalization
#To determine how the print tip and location affected the measure so it is a 
#physical normalization procedure...

#Extract the location using regular expressions
probeLayout <- RG_corrected$genes |>
  as_tibble() |>
  extract(
    Spot,
    into = c("GridRow", "GridCol", "SpotNumber"),
    regex = "R(\\d+)\\s*-\\s*C(\\d+)\\s*:\\s*(\\d+)",
    remove = FALSE,
    convert = TRUE
  )

head(probeLayout)

#Obtain the order of the spots because we need to give them to limma in a certain order:
#Spots were sorted by grid row, grid column, and spot number to group 
#each print-tip's 945 spots consecutively.

spotOrder <- probeLayout |>
  arrange(GridRow, GridCol, SpotNumber) |>
  pull(ID)

#This simultaneously reorders the fluorescence matrices and the gene annotation.
#We do it directly on the object
RG_corrected <- RG_corrected[spotOrder, ]

#Internal dimensions of 21 × 45, 2 columns, 12 rows
printLayout <- list(
  ngrid.r = 12,
  ngrid.c = 2,
  nspot.r = 21,
  nspot.c = 45
)

#Authors  excluded control probes from the normalization so we assign weights
#to use later
normalizationWeights <- if_else(
  RG_corrected$genes$FLAG == 0,
  1,
  0
)
normalizationWeights[1:20]


#We don't normalize, but use it to obtain the values to compare with normalized.
#M is log2 ratio and A is average intensity
MA_before <- RG_corrected |>
  normalizeWithinArrays(
    method = "none",
    bc.method = "none"
  )

#Here we do the print tip loess normalization... and obtain M and A values
MA <- RG_corrected |>
  normalizeWithinArrays(
    layout = printLayout,
    method = "printtiploess",
    weights = normalizationWeights,
    bc.method = "none"
  )

#Merge the two data sets (before and after) for subsequent graph comparison...
MAplotData <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    M = MA_before$M[, 1],
    A = MA_before$A[, 1],
    Processing = "Before"
  ),
  tibble(
    M = MA$M[, 1],
    A = MA$A[, 1],
    Processing = "After"
  )
)

#Plot both graphs side by side
MAplotData |>
  mutate(
    Processing = factor(
      Processing,
      levels = c("Before", "After")
    ),
    FLAG = rep(MA$genes$FLAG, 2)#Put the FLAG vector two times to fill the table...and remove control values in plot
  ) |>
  filter(FLAG == 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = A, y = M)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "red") +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    formula = y ~ x,
    color = "blue",
    se = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Processing) +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r}

#OBTAIN THE EXPRESSION MATRIX

#The authors had discrepancies in their labels between the the G and the R
#so we capture the log2FoldChange and invert it to get the right values...
dim(MA$M)
expressionMatrix <- -MA$M

#We label the expression accordingly... to the ID (it was changed during 
#normalization)
rownames(expressionMatrix) <- MA$genes$ID

#Here we sort it back to the original order in which it was given...
expressionMatrix <- expressionMatrix |>
  data.frame() |> 
  arrange(as.numeric(rownames(expressionMatrix))) |> 
  as.matrix()

#Matrix dimensions check
dim(expressionMatrix)

write.csv(
  expressionMatrix,
  file = "../_raw/OURmicroarrayData.csv",
  row.names = TRUE
)

```

```{r}
#COMPRARE TO THEIR RESULTS
GSE24504 <- getGEO("GSE24504")
publishedExpression <- exprs(GSE24504[[1]])


#Verify same rows and columns
stopifnot(
  all(rownames(expressionMatrix) ==
        rownames(publishedExpression)),

  all(colnames(expressionMatrix) ==
        colnames(publishedExpression))
)

#We make a tibble that one column is the SampleID (122 samples)
#The other column is their correlation coefficient... so we isolate column
#by column (each sample) and compare with the same sample foldchange values
#and calculate the correlation between samples....
validation <- tibble(
  SampleID = colnames(expressionMatrix),

  Correlation = map_dbl(
    seq_len(ncol(expressionMatrix)),
    ~ cor(
      expressionMatrix[, .x],
      publishedExpression[, .x]
    )
  )
)

#Summary of the data... (very high mean and median)
summary(validation$Correlation)

#We do a histogran to see how our data is distributed
validation |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Correlation)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20) +
  theme_minimal()

#Finally... we compare all the expression values of only the first sample...
#and we can see that their pearson correlation is probably close to 1. 
#It means that the values highly resemble the other data...
tibble(
  Ours = expressionMatrix[, 1],
  Published = publishedExpression[, 1]
) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Published, y = Ours)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    color = "red"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
